subject.title: Heartbeat skipped reason 'target-none' is misleading when delivery is disabled by default

question: Should the heartbeat disabled-delivery path keep `reason: "target-none"` and add a human-readable hint/status message, or should the machine reason itself be renamed?
rationale: The source-reproducible confusion is real, but the remaining fix changes operator-facing diagnostics and possibly the machine-readable heartbeat event contract, so automation should not choose the permanent contract shape alone.

options.title: Add hint, keep reason
options.body: Keep `reason: "target-none"` as the machine contract and add a human-readable disabled-delivery hint or CLI/status rendering.

options.title: Rename reason
options.body: Rename the machine reason to an explicit configuration-related code and accept the compatibility risk for private parsers.

options.title: Docs only
options.body: Leave runtime output unchanged and document that `target-none` means delivery is disabled by configuration.

recommendation.title: Add hint, keep reason
recommendation.body: Keep `reason: "target-none"` as the machine contract and add a human-readable disabled-delivery hint or CLI/status rendering.

likelyOwner.reason: The default-disabled heartbeat behavior and latest current-line ownership both trace most strongly to `@steipete`.
